reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3, E4) demonstrates the covariance-based Gaussian method for vibrational entropy in elemental solids and one high-entropy alloy, but only in the solid state and without addressing fluid-phase adaptation, diffusive corrections, or fusion property predictions. The key premises about fluid-phase applicability, cost reduction, and accuracy for fusion properties are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Short AIMD/MC trajectories (5–10 ps) generate sufficient atomic displacement data to capture anharmonicity and electron–vibration coupling.
A Gaussian approximation to the displacement covariance matrix yields effective vibrational frequencies that embed these effects.
The method can be adapted to fluid phases by accounting for diffusive motion, providing faithful free energies.
The approach reduces computational cost by at least an order of magnitude versus explicit AIMD or TOR-TILD.
The method is valid for multicomponent high-entropy alloys near fusion conditions.
